evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Who to tell, in what order, and what each one needs.' plus subhead 'a checklist for adult children settling a parent's affairs in England and Wales' says what, who and where in two lines; the button 'Copy my checklist' has an object and the line under it says exactly what it does.
evidence.fit: Calm, practical, never sells: the only first-screen action is a free copy of the list ('Nothing to sign up for'). England and Wales and 'not legal advice' appear in the example label in the first screen and get their own section. The brief's tension (collect interest, nowhere to send it) is resolved honestly but weakly: the email form only saves to localStorage, so as founder I collect nothing, and the 'not ready yet' section sits fifth, after letters and scope.
evidence.distinctiveness: The artifact is the product: 'Tick what they had. The list puts itself in order.' chips rebuild a numbered list with 'Have ready' document tags and italic 'letter' marks; the three document cards (death certificate, Tell Us Once reference, grant of probate stamped 'Comes later') and the dotted-blank bank letter are specific to estate admin. Structure is still a familiar hero + sections pattern.
evidence.proof: The working checklist is in the first screen at 1440 (right column) and starts within the first screen at 390. Ticking 'A car' added 'Their car insurer' and 'DVLA, about the car' and changed the Tell Us Once line to 'Cancels their driving licence (the car itself is line 10)', which is correct; summary updated 11 -> 14 to contact, 4 -> 5 certified copies, 6 -> 9 letters. Labelled 'Example:' at the top. It answers my first doubt as an executor: what do I do first and what do I need in hand.
evidence.craft: Clean type scale (serif display, sans body), consistent rules and spacing, no overflow at 320/390/768/1440 (probe 0px), smallest text 12px only on small tags. Copy status appears directly under the button pressed. Dense in places: at 390 the chips with two-line labels are 73px tall and the list lines carry three tag pills each, which reads busy at night on a phone.
evidence.mobile: 390: H1, subhead and 'Copy my checklist' (48px) fit the first screen, chips begin at the bottom; chips 54-73px, nav links 44px, no overflow. But the page runs ~7,900px and the checklist alone ~3,000px, and the hero 'Copy' button sits above the chips, so tapping it before customising copies the example parent's 11 lines. Nav is a simple wrapped row, works.
evidence.honesty: Example label is visible beside the artifact at every width; sample letter says 'Sample letter, written for this page'; email form says 'Nothing is sent. It stays on this page, in this browser.' before submit and 'Saved in this browser only. Nothing has been sent' after. Deduction: 'Settle is not ready yet' is only in the fifth section (~6,800px down at 390) and the footer; the hero speaks in present tense and the summary says '6 come with a letter in Settle', so a cold reader can believe the product exists until far down.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390 (touch): every chip toggles with visible state, list and live summary update with a highlight on new lines; 'Start again' restored defaults (11/4/6); all chips off leaves 5 lines and '0 come with a letter'; both Owned and Rented shows insurer, mortgage and landlord. Both 'Copy my checklist' buttons put a plain-text list on the clipboard with 'Copied. 11 lines are on your clipboard' beside the button; a fallback textarea exists. Email form: empty -> 'Type an email address first. Nothing was saved.', 'foo' -> 'That does not look like an email address', valid -> saved message. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Specific and plain: 'Ask for the bereavement team', 'Redirecting the post to you catches the accounts nobody knew about', 'A call with the right one in front of you is one call, not three', 'you do not write the sentence about your parent's death over and over'. Slightly procedural and repetitive ('Nothing has been sent' three times); warmth is quieter than B's.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: specific promise, named audience and region, an operable example list with counts, and a button whose label matches what it does. 390: promise and action are in view and the example box heading starts at the bottom, but the chips and lines are below the fold, and nothing in the first viewport says the product is not available yet.

problems: 'Settle is not ready yet' is buried in the fifth section; the hero and the summary line ('6 come with a letter in Settle') read as if the product exists today.
The interest form saves only to this browser, so the founder collects no interest at all, and the visitor is asked to type an email that goes nowhere.
At 390 the page is ~7,900px and dense with tag pills; the hero 'Copy my checklist' sits above the chips, so tapping it first copies the example parent's list, not hers.

evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: H1 'Everyone you need to tell, in the order to tell them.' and the lede 'Settle is a checklist that takes it one contact at a time... and a letter you can send to each' plus 'England and Wales' in the header; 'It isn't ready yet' is right under the lede. A stranger could repeat it.
evidence.fit: Tone is the best fit for a grieving reader: unhurried serif, 'Most of it can wait longer than you'd think', 'If you're reading this in the first weeks, there's no hurry.' The legal-advice and England-and-Wales box sits in the first screen. But the brief's constraint 'nowhere to send sign-ups yet' is not reflected: the form promises 'we'll send one message when Settle opens' and confirms 'We'll write once', while the code only writes to localStorage (SIGNUP_ENDPOINT = ''). It also sends readers to citizensadvice.org.uk, deathnotificationservice.co.uk and gov.uk, none supplied by the brief.
evidence.distinctiveness: Single narrow column of a book-like serif, a manila-tinted letter inside a sample contact card, italic time groupings ('In the first few days', 'In the first fortnight'). Calm and appropriate, but structurally a plain long-form page; the only product-specific artifact is a static list and one contact card.
evidence.proof: The list ('The first fortnight, the way Settle lays it out') starts at ~780px at 390 and below the first screen at 1440. It is fixed (8 items, not tailored to what the parent had); ticking works and persists. The bank contact page shows what they'll ask for, what happens next and a letter, which is good evidence of the product, but it is static and includes unsourced figures ('Takes about twenty minutes on the phone, or ten in a branch', 'each costs a little over ten pounds').
evidence.craft: Consistent rhythm, generous line height, embedded licensed font, tinted disclaimer box, checkbox tick animation; no overflow (probe 0px), smallest text 15px. Minor: H2 'The first fortnight, the way Settle lays it out' leaves 'out' orphaned on its own line at 1440; the 1440 layout is a 36rem column with large empty margins.
evidence.mobile: Composed for the phone: 390 shows promise, not-ready line and the disclaimer in the first screen; checklist rows are 105-178px tall tap targets; ticks are remembered on reload ('2 of 8 done' survived reload); after submitting, the confirmation replaced the form in place at y=373 of 844. Cost: the action is ~4,990px down and the artifact starts below the first screen.
evidence.honesty: 390/1440: entered jane@example.co.uk, tapped 'Tell me when it's ready'; the page showed 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' Nothing was sent; it was written to localStorage only, and nothing before the click said so (the intro says 'Leave your email and we'll send one message'). For a grieving reader this is a promise the company cannot keep. Unsourced figures in the sample ('about twenty minutes on the phone', 'Five or six copies is usual; each costs a little over ten pounds'). To its credit, 'It isn't ready yet' and 'not legal advice' are in the first screen.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440, 768 and 390: each checkbox ticks with animation and hides its detail; tally reads 'Nothing ticked yet. That's fine.' -> '2 of 8 done.' -> 'All 8 done. Everything else can wait a while.'; 'Clear the ticks' reset to zero; state persisted across reload. Empty and 'foo' submissions show 'That doesn't look like an email address. Could you check it?'. Deductions: the sign-up reports success for a send that does not happen; three outbound links go to destinations the brief did not supply and cannot be checked here.
evidence.copy: Written, not defaulted, and kind without gloom: 'After a parent dies, the paperwork arrives all at once', 'Nothing ticked yet. That's fine.', 'Scotland and Northern Ireland have different rules, and we'd rather not guess at them.', 'Nothing before then, and nothing after.' The 'What it is, and what it isn't' list is specific. Undercut only by the false 'We'll write once'.
evidence.first_screen: 1440 and 390: a specific promise for a named situation and an early disclaimer, but no artifact or example in view and no action in view: the only action is described as 'at the bottom of this page', and the only link in view goes to Citizens Advice. Nothing in the viewport makes the promise believable beyond the words.

problems: The sign-up confirms 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' although the brief says there is nowhere to send sign-ups and the code only stores the email in this browser: a false promise to a grieving visitor.
The checklist is a fixed sample below the first screen and does not adapt to what the parent had, so the first screens prove the idea with words, not the product.

Unsourced figures presented as fact (about twenty minutes on the phone, five or six copies usual, a little over ten pounds each) and outbound links (Citizens Advice, Death Notification Service, GOV.UK) the brief did not supply.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The page's only conversion action, the email form the hero points to ('there's a place to leave your email at the bottom of this page'), reports success that did not happen. After submitting a valid address it shows 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' The script has SIGNUP_ENDPOINT = '' and only pushes the email into localStorage 'settle-interest'; no request is made. Nothing before the click says the email is not sent; the intro says 'Leave your email and we'll send one message when Settle opens'. The brief states 'there is nowhere to send sign-ups yet'.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P004/B/index.html from disk at 390x844 (or 1440x900). Scroll to 'If you'd like to know when it's ready'. Type jane@example.co.uk and press 'Tell me when it's ready'. The confirmation 'Thank you. We'll write once, when Settle is ready.' appears; in DevTools, Network shows no request and localStorage['settle-interest'] holds the address. See B/index.html lines 318, 328-329 and 388-418.

reason: As the executor on her phone at night, A gives me something useful at once: tick what Dad had and get an ordered list of who to call and what to have ready, which I can copy, with nothing to sign up for. B is gentler in tone, but it ends by telling a grieving visitor 'We'll write once' when nothing is sent, and as founder I would not put my name to that. Two things would change my mind: B making its sign-up honest and putting a tailored list near the top, or A turning out to collect nothing a founder could use.
